title: Best ENERGY STAR Dehumidifiers (2026): Most Efficient Ranked
h1: The Best ENERGY STAR Dehumidifiers, Ranked by Real Efficiency
dek: Nearly every dehumidifier wears an ENERGY STAR sticker. These are the ones that pull the most water per kilowatt-hour on the certified numbers.
description: The best ENERGY STAR dehumidifiers of 2026, ranked on certified IEF and rated kWh per year — the most energy efficient picks, not box claims or nameplate watts.
intro: Walk down any appliance aisle and almost every portable unit is an **ENERGY STAR dehumidifier** — the blue logo is on nearly everything, which makes it useless as a tiebreaker. The number that actually separates a frugal machine from a thirsty one is the **Integrated Energy Factor (IEF)**: liters of water removed per kilowatt-hour, measured under the Department of Energy’s standard test.

There’s also a stricter tier, **ENERGY STAR Most Efficient**, reserved for the highest-scoring models in each size class. Between the IEF and ENERGY STAR’s rated kWh per year, you can compare any two certified models on equal footing — something you can’t do with the pint claims printed on boxes, which some brands measure in hot, swampy conditions that inflate the number.

We ranked this list on ENERGY STAR’s certified-product data. If you want the full cost math, our guide to [how much electricity a dehumidifier uses](/guides/how-much-electricity-does-a-dehumidifier-use/) walks through it.
topPicksLead: On the certified numbers, the **AEOCKY Leo-003** is the most energy efficient portable dehumidifier most homes can buy, rated 2.21 liters per kWh and one of only nine models in its class to earn Most Efficient status.

products.whyWeLoveIt: This is the rare mainstream Amazon dehumidifier that beats Midea and Frigidaire on certified efficiency. It shares an ENERGY STAR listing with AEOCKY's pump-free Leo-Lite3, so you get the same Most Efficient rating — plus a pump that sends condensate up and out when there's no floor drain nearby.
products.performance: ENERGY STAR rates the chassis at 44.94 pints a day under DOE conditions at 2.21 L/kWh, for 438 kWh a year. Only nine of 273 certified portables in the 25.01–50 pint class meet the Most Efficient bar, and this is one of them. The “140 pint” on the box is measured at 95°F and 95% humidity, so size it as a 45-pint machine. AEOCKY includes a 5-meter hose and says the pump passed more than 10,000 reliability cycles. Our [best AEOCKY dehumidifier](/best/best-aeocky-dehumidifier/) guide maps every model name to its certified rating.
products.notes: If there's a drain lower than the unit, you can skip the pump and run a gravity hose instead.

blocks.text: ENERGY STAR’s Version 6.0 rules, in effect since October 1, 2025, set minimums of 1.70 L/kWh for portables up to 25 pints, 2.01 for 25.01–50 pints and 3.30 above that. Ducted whole-home units need 2.22 to 3.81 depending on case size. The federal legal minimum for the middle class is lower still, at 1.60.

sections.heading: How we pick energy efficient dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We don’t lab-test, and for efficiency we don’t need to: ENERGY STAR publishes certified IEF, DOE capacity and rated kWh per year for every listed model, all measured the same way. We ranked on those figures, then checked manuals for drainage and operating range, and read owner reviews for reliability problems that would cancel out any savings.
We ignored box capacity claims and nameplate wattage entirely. A label reading 8.5 amps at 115 volts (about 978 watts) describes a wiring maximum, not what the machine actually draws while running.

sections.heading: What to look for in an energy efficient dehumidifier

items.label: The IEF, not just the logo
items.text: Every certified unit clears a minimum. Look up the actual liters-per-kWh rating in ENERGY STAR’s public dataset.

items.label: The DOE pint rating
items.text: Some brands, AEOCKY and Waykar among them, headline capacity at 95°F and 95% humidity — roughly three times the DOE figure measured at 65°F and 60%.

items.label: Rated kWh per year
items.text: This is the closest thing to a bill estimate, and it’s measured identically across brands.

items.label: The right size for the room
items.text: An oversized compressor short-cycles and wastes its efficiency edge. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) helps you match pints to square feet.

items.label: Easy filter access
items.text: A clogged filter or dusty coil makes the fan and compressor work harder. Keep up with basic [dehumidifier maintenance](/guides/dehumidifier-maintenance/).

sections.heading: Do dehumidifiers use a lot of electricity?

blocks.text: Not as much as most people fear. A certified 50-pint-class portable is rated at roughly 440–520 kWh a year, and a small-room unit closer to 285. That’s real money over a humid season, but far less than a central air conditioner — and the gap between an average and a top-rated model is smaller still.

Less than the marketing implies, but it’s real. At the EIA’s August 2026 average residential rate of 18.44 cents per kWh, the AEOCKY Leo-003’s rated 438 kWh costs about $81 a year, versus about $95 for a Midea Cube 50’s 515 kWh — a gap of roughly $14.

blocks.title: Don’t overpay for a small saving
blocks.text: A Most Efficient model with a pump can cost a couple hundred dollars more upfront than a standard ENERGY STAR unit — and save only about $14 a year. Buy efficiency where the unit will run hardest: crawl spaces, basements and whole-house systems.

items: **Bigger always wastes more.** Not per liter. Larger compressors are usually more efficient, which is why the DOE sets higher bars for bigger classes. AEOCKY’s big chassis beats its own small Rhea-001 on liters per kWh.

**Desiccant means efficient.** Renewable silica units draw no power while working, but they move very little water. Electric rotary desiccants use a heater and cost more per pint than a good compressor model — buy one for cold spaces, not savings. Our [best desiccant dehumidifier](/best/best-desiccant-dehumidifier/) guide explains when they make sense.

**Unplugging saves money.** Mold can start growing on damp materials within 24 to 48 hours, per the EPA. An efficient unit you leave running beats a power-hungry one you switch off to protect the bill.

blocks.text: On ENERGY STAR’s certified numbers, the **AEOCKY Leo-003** is the most efficient portable dehumidifier for most homes, and the **Rhea-001** is the efficient pick for a single room. Choose the **Midea Cube 50** if you want more water per day from an established brand and can accept about $14 a year in extra electricity. For crawl spaces and ducted systems that run all season, the **Santa Fe Compact70** and **Aprilaire E080** are where efficiency pays off fastest.

faqs.q: What is the most energy efficient ENERGY STAR dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Among portables, AEOCKY’s 140-pint-class chassis (sold as the Leo-Lite3, Rhea-003 and Leo-003) is rated 2.21 L/kWh and meets ENERGY STAR’s Most Efficient criteria. For a ducted whole-house system, the Aprilaire E080 leads at 2.35 L/kWh.

faqs.q: What does ENERGY STAR Most Efficient mean on a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: It’s a tier above standard certification for the top performers in each capacity class. In ENERGY STAR’s current data, every Most Efficient portable in the 25.01–50 pint class is rated at least 2.20 L/kWh, versus the 2.01 minimum for basic certification.

faqs.q: Do dehumidifiers use a lot of electricity?
faqs.a: Moderately. ENERGY STAR rates large portables at roughly 440–520 kWh a year and small-room models around 285 kWh — on the order of $50 to $95 a year at 18.44 cents per kWh. See our [electricity use guide](/guides/how-much-electricity-does-a-dehumidifier-use/) for the full math.

faqs.q: How much does an efficient dehumidifier save per year?
faqs.a: Comparing a 438 kWh/yr model with a 515 kWh/yr model, the difference is about $14 a year at 18.44 cents per kWh. Savings are bigger for units that run most of the season, like crawl space and whole-house systems.

faqs.q: Why is the pint rating on the box higher than ENERGY STAR’s?
faqs.a: Some brands measure capacity at 95°F and 95% humidity, which inflates the figure. The DOE test uses 65°F and 60%, which reflects a typical basement. Compare DOE pints to DOE pints.

faqs.q: Are desiccant dehumidifiers more energy efficient?
faqs.a: Not for whole rooms. Renewable mini desiccants use no power while absorbing but remove very little water. Electric desiccant units run a heater and usually cost more per pint than a good compressor model, though they work better in cold spaces.

faqs.q: Does a bigger dehumidifier use more electricity?
faqs.a: It draws more power, but it usually removes more water per kWh and runs for shorter stretches. What predicts your bill is the IEF and rated kWh per year, not the capacity printed on the box.
